football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 1.3 points.
supporting: When UCLA has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): UCLA’s offense has allowed a sack on 4.5% of its dropbacks, and Nevada’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.0% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
When UCLA has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): UCLA’s offense averages 7.9 yards per pass attempt, and Nevada’s defense allows 5.5 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).

When Nevada has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Nevada’s offense has allowed a sack on 4.4% of its dropbacks, and UCLA’s defense sacks the quarterback on 6.1% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
contradicting: When UCLA has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): UCLA’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 13.8% of its runs, and Nevada’s defense stops 12.8% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
When Nevada has the ball (third down): Nevada’s offense converts 39.5% of its third downs, and UCLA’s defense allows opponents to convert 22.4% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

When Nevada has the ball (big plays on the ground): Nevada’s offense turns 5.9% of its runs into explosive gains, and UCLA’s defense gives up explosive gains on 2.8% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Nevada has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Nevada’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 19.3% of its runs, and UCLA’s defense stops 21.9% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).

Carter Jones has completed 53 of 89 passes (59.6%) for 654 yards, 7.3 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in four games for Nevada, and has been sacked on 7 of 96 dropbacks.
